measurement.name: Atlantic South Equatorial Undercurrent
measurement.range_interpretation: One approximate author-reported 20 cm/s core width. Abstract approximately 100 km is separate unreconciled context, not an endpoint, error or independent occupation.
measurement.geographic_scope: Eastern and western Atlantic sections: approximately 25–29 W and 4 W, within the 1978–1980 study. Not the newer 35 W ledger section or the entire current.
measurement.section_orientation: Source cross-current sections; no geographic edge pair or exact flow-normal projection extracted.
measurement.layer: Subthermocline 20 cm/s isotach core. Reported core depths and vertical extent are context, not fixed width-layer limits.
measurement.time_convention: Author summary across six 1978–1980 cruises. Individual figure dates do not date this characteristic width; no per-cruise or seasonal width series extracted.
measurement.boundary_rule: Source defines the core as flow within the 20 cm/s isotach and reports about 120 km core width. This is not the net-flow boundary.
measurement.source_citation: Molinari, R. L., Voituriez, B., and Duncan, P. (1981), Observations in the subthermocline undercurrent of the Equatorial South Atlantic Ocean: 1978–1980, Oceanologica Acta 4(4), 451–456.
measurement.source_locator: Printed p453/PDF p3, core definition and width paragraphs; abstract p451/PDF p1; methods/captions p452/PDF p2; net-flow boundary limitation p456/PDF p6.
measurement.extraction_method: Transcribed the explicit contour-defined body core width after original-page review; no figure digitization or geographic edge inference.
measurement.source_quality_note: Body about 120 km versus abstract about 100 km retained separately. Reference captions use 1000 db while prose uses 1000 m. Numerical width uncertainty and net-flow boundaries unknown.
remaining_gates: Resolve source approximate-width description discrepancy without manufacturing a range.
Recover paired geographic edges and compatible repeated sections before mapping or annual variability.
